_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Kalyan Jewellers (consolidated, ₹ crore). Segment-driven revenue (India, Middle East, Candere); valued on a 15-year DCF.

segments.name: India (Kalyan showrooms)
segments._why: Q1FY27 +38% and Q2FY27 +27% (ex-bullion) on the gold price; H2 faces a very high base (Q4FY26 +68%), the May-2026 duty hike and the PM's appeal to defer gold buying, so we assume ~12% in H2. FY28-29: ~85 franchise stores a year (~20% store growth) plus mid-single-digit same-store growth.
segments._marginWhy: 6.8% in FY26; 5.9% in Q1FY27 including a ₹41 cr one-off duty gain (5.1% underlying). Franchise (FOCO) stores share margin with partners, and gold-exchange sales dilute margin by 20-30bp. We assume ~6%, below FY26.

segments.name: Middle East
segments._why: Q1FY27 +29%, Q2FY27 +12%. Store count flat at 38; growth is mostly the gold price and same-store sales.

segments.name: Candere (online + stores)
segments._why: Q2FY27 +64%; ~50 new stores in FY27 (138 at Sep-26).
segments._marginWhy: Turned marginally profitable in H2FY26; EBITDA not disclosed. We assume a slow climb.

_unallocLabel: Reconciling items: other operating income less eliminations (negative = adds to EBITDA)
_unallocWhy: FY26 reported EBITDA (₹2,562 cr, Screener) exceeds the sum of segment EBITDA (₹2,412 cr) by ~₹150 cr: other operating income (royalty from franchisees), less inter-segment eliminations.
_capexWhy: Cash capex below ₹250 cr a year (ICRA) because franchise partners fund new stores; plus lease principal (~₹280 cr in FY26), since rent sits below EBITDA under Ind AS 116.
_depWhy: Q1FY27 depreciation ₹115 cr (~₹470 cr a year) ≈ 9.7% of gross block.
_treasuryWhy: Net debt, so no treasury income; other income is entered separately.
_otherIncomeWhy: FY26 normal other income ₹208 cr (interest on deposits, misc.); FY27 includes part of the ₹102 cr non-core land sale.
_interestWhy: FY26 ₹499 cr; Q1FY27 ₹108 cr. Non-gold-loan debt in India fully repaid by Sep-2026; gold metal loans (~₹3,600 cr) remain and cost more as the gold price rises.

dcf._betaWhy: Discretionary spend tied to gold prices; market-like sensitivity.
dcf._tgWhy: Jewellery demand tracks nominal GDP and the gold price; 6% allows for slowing volumes as gold gets dearer.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Asset-light franchise model keeps capex low.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Gold stays high and demand holds; franchise roll-out of 90+ stores a year continues; India margin back to ~6.8% as cash-for-gold and studded mix help.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Higher duty and a falling gold price hit value growth; franchise dilution pushes India margin to ~5.3%; growth slows to low teens.

operatingDebt.label: Gold metal loans (inventory funding)
operatingDebt._why: Gold borrowed from banks to stock showrooms, repaid in gold; ~10% of revenue at Mar-26. Treated as working-capital funding (as the company, ICRA and brokers do), not as financing debt.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Kalyan (Jefferies, Citi, MOFSL, BOBCAPS all use P/E on 2028 EPS). 30x = Kalyan's 40x median one-year-forward P/E since 2023, cut by the 24% sector de-rating (Titan at 65x vs its 86x five-year median). Bull 36x (half the de-rating), bear 24x (Kalyan's 2023 levels).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, Ke 12.5%, terminal growth 6%. Thin margins and inventory keep free cash low, so the DCF sits below the market multiples.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Adjusts for debt. 17x Sep-28E EBITDA is consistent with 30x P/E after interest and tax; Kalyan trades at 20.5x trailing today (30x median since 2023).
